title: Mitsuko Uchida's divine Beethoven
gist: A short three-part culture notebook by Paul Lay: Mitsuko Uchida's new Suntory Hall recording of Beethoven's final three piano sonatas (Ops 109-111), Djibril Diop Mambéty's 1973 Senegalese film Touki Bouki, and Nick Lloyd's history The Eastern Front. The one claim with wider reach is Lay's assertion that a striking share of today's geopolitical troubles trace directly back to the First World War — and specifically to its eastern, not western, theatre.

themes.theme: First World War's eastern theatre as the root of modern conflict

insights.claim: A large share of contemporary geopolitical troubles trace directly back to the disaster of the First World War, a lineage the author finds persistently bewildering.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: Supports treating the 1914-18 settlement, not 1945, as the origin point when mapping the deep causes of today's Eastern European and Middle Eastern conflicts.
insights.quote: It remains bewildering that so many current travails are rooted in the disaster of the First World War.

insights.claim: Popular and scholarly attention to the First World War over-weights trench warfare in the West, while the decisive terrain was the vast landscape between Germany and Russia including the Balkans, the font of the conflict.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: Reframes the standard WWI narrative toward the Russo-German and Balkan space — the same corridor generating today's security risk.
insights.quote: takes us away from the understandable preponderance of interest in the trench warfare of the West

insights.claim: On the Eastern Front the fighting resembled older wars of pitched battles and Cannae-like pincer movements but intensified by technology, collapsing great empires and stoking enduring hatreds.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: A model for how new technology grafted onto classical manoeuvre warfare produces regime collapse — a lens applicable to current drone-era conflicts.
insights.quote: war was more reminiscent of past struggles of pitched battles and Cannae-like pincer movements, but intensified by technology

insights.claim: Djibril Diop Mambéty's 1973 Senegalese film Touki Bouki was only truly recognised as a masterpiece after Martin Scorsese's 2008 restoration, 35 years after its release.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: An example of how canonisation and value in cultural markets depend on a later gatekeeper's endorsement rather than on the work's intrinsic quality at launch.
insights.quote: though its greatness was only truly recognised following Martin Scorsese’s restoration of it in 2008
insights.locator: Touki Bouki: masterpiece of African cinema

insights.claim: Beethoven's final piano sonatas anticipate jazz — the syncopated rhythms of the second movement of Op. 111 prefigure a genre that arrived roughly a century later.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: Minor, but illustrates the author's recurring interest in how innovations are legible only in hindsight.
insights.quote: listen to the syncopated rhythms of the second movement of the final sonata, which anticipate jazz
insights.locator: These are among the greatest, most innovative pieces of music ever written

insights.claim: Mitsuko Uchida, in her late seventies, recorded Beethoven's Ops 109-111 in Tokyo's Suntory Hall in October, the same month the author heard her perform the programme at London's Wigmore Hall.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: Context only — a release note on a recording the author rates as near-definitive.
insights.locator: Last October I was lucky to be within the intimacy
